title: Ramp's cards: token spend rose 1.5% in late summer, after 42% in July
friendlyTitle: Ramp's cards show AI use rising while the bill barely moved
summary: TechCrunch reports that Ramp's card data shows companies using more AI without spending much more on it. Token spend grew 1.5% across August and September, after a 42% rise in July. From 23 September to 23 October it rose 8.9%, which Ramp's lead economist Ara Kharazian calls a re-acceleration, while saying the headwinds on spend are still strong. He told TechCrunch that almost all of the AI spend on Ramp's cards comes from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies. The top 1% of firms, which had been near $10,000 per employee per month at the summer peak, came in just below that in August and September. Median firms spend $12 to $15 per employee per month. The top 10% spend $600 to $1,000. Kharazian points to price cuts and to customers getting better at caps, routers, and cheaper models, not to a collapse in use. TechCrunch says OpenAI halved API prices for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in September, and that Anthropic has said in a recent filing that cuts on Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 reduced revenue growth by about $600 million. These are Ramp's customers, not the whole economy.
friendlySummary: TechCrunch reports that Ramp's card data shows companies using more AI without spending much more. A token is a small piece of text the model reads or writes, and labs often bill by the token. Spending on tokens grew 1.5% across August and September, after a 42% rise in July. From 23 September to 23 October it rose 8.9%. Ramp's lead economist, Ara Kharazian, calls that a pickup, and still says the pressure against higher bills is strong. He told TechCrunch that almost all of the AI spend on these cards comes from venture-backed, fast-growing tech companies. The top 1% of firms had been near $10,000 per employee per month at the summer peak, and came in just under that in August and September. A typical firm spends $12 to $15 per employee per month. The top 10% spend $600 to $1,000. He points to price cuts, and to customers getting better at limits and cheaper models, not to people stopping. TechCrunch says OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in September, and that Anthropic has said in a recent filing that price cuts on two models reduced revenue growth by about $600 million. These are Ramp's customers, not every company.
whyItMatters: If your team is being judged on tokens used, Ramp's chart is the counterexample: volume can rise while the bill does not. The practical check is your own invoice against last month, not the industry total. A median of $12 to $15 per employee is a different business from the firms spending near $10,000. Do not budget as if you are in the top 1%.
